heard: Spacecraft never dodged giant rocks while crossing the asteroid belt. On January 1, 1801, astronomer G.U. Sepp Piazzi discovered the first fragment, Ceres, while hunting for a missing planet. An informal group called the Celestial Police formed to search for this predicted missing world. Instead of a single planet, they found a vast graveyard of planetesimals prevented from merging by Jupiter's massive gravity. The average distance between these space Space rocks is about 600,000 miles, making the belt an extreme cosmic desert. Spacecraft safely cruise through because the probability of hitting an asteroid is less than one in a billion. Spacecraft never dodge giant rocks while crossing the asteroid belt.
